questions.explain: Filterable attributes (anything in a WHERE clause) become columns — indexable, sargable, constrainable; descriptive attributes stay in metadata JSON; promote JSON paths to columns when they start appearing in filters.
options: Store everything in JSON columns
Store everything as relational columns
Columns for filterable attributes, JSON for descriptive attributes; promote JSON paths to columns when they appear in filters
Metadata filtering is not possible with vector search
questions.q: How should filterable metadata be designed?

questions.explain: The (@param IS NULL OR column = @param) pattern gives one procedure for all filter combinations; OPTION (RECOMPILE) defeats parameter sniffing since a fresh plan per filter combination is worth the trivial compile cost.
options: One procedure with NULL-able filter parameters plus OPTION (RECOMPILE)
A separate procedure per filter combination
Dynamic SQL without any plan caching concerns
Client-side filtering after fetching all chunks
questions.q: How does the chapter handle combinatorial filter parameters without plan-cache problems?

questions.explain: An EXISTS semi-join filters without duplicating chunk rows (a JOIN would multiply rows for multi-group documents); a visibility flag lets tenant-public documents skip the permission check.
options: A JOIN through the permissions table
No permission filtering needed with RLS
Filtering in the application after retrieval
An EXISTS semi-join (not a JOIN), with a visibility flag to skip checks for tenant-public documents
questions.q: What is the right shape for permission-aware vector retrieval?

questions.explain: Freshness works better as a soft boost blended into the ranking score than as a hard filter — slightly older authoritative documents can still surface; tune the coefficient so recency doesn't beat relevance.
options: Always hard-filter to the last 30 days
Blend recency as a soft score boost rather than a hard filter
Ignore publish dates entirely
Delete old documents from the corpus
questions.q: How should freshness/recency be handled in ranking?

questions.explain: Filter-first wins when filters are highly selective; vector-first wins when filters are weak; encode the heuristic in the procedure (selective under ~10% → pre-filter into a temp table) and log the chosen strategy per query.
options: Always filter first
Always vector-search first
Encode the selectivity heuristic in the procedure and log the chosen strategy per query
Let the user choose the order
questions.q: How is the filter-first vs. vector-first execution order decided?
